summary:
## Core Finesse Build Concepts

The primary philosophy of a Finesse build is to control the battlefield through debuffs and high-damage critical strikes.

- **Ranged Focus**: Pure Finesse builds naturally favor ranged combat, with significant bonuses directed towards **Longbows**.
- **Poison & Bleed Strategy**: The core combat loop involves stacking **poisons** and **bleeds** on enemies. These damage-over-time effects are amplified by Finesse gear and abilities, and they enable powerful follow-up attacks with skills like **Executioner**.

## Destiny Paths & Hybrids

Your choice of Destiny defines your build's primary strengths.

- **Pure Finesse (Nightblade)**: The capstone destiny requires 109 points in Finesse. Its main feature is **Assassination**, granting a +300% damage guaranteed critical hit after an **Evasion**.
  > [!IMPORTANT]
  > Evasion is an RNG-based mechanic with a maximum chance of around 17%. This makes the build's highest damage potential inconsistent and unreliable.
- **Finesse/Might Hybrid**: This offers a more balanced approach between melee and ranged combat, providing melee damage bonuses that pure Finesse lacks. It's also superior for stealth attacks. A recommended strategy is to use the **Assassin** destiny (one tier below Nightblade) and invest the saved points into **Might** for perks like **Concussive Force**, which synergizes perfectly with stuns from Finesse traps.
- **Finesse/Sorcery Hybrid**: This path is ideal for a **100% ranged build** (Bow + Staff/Scepter/Chakrams) or to add **elemental damage** to Finesse weapons. The **Spellcloak** destiny is a strong choice, offering guaranteed crits on panicked enemies (a status effect applied by fire spells).
  > [!NOTE]
  > It's often more effective to build primarily into Sorcery and take a smaller dip into Finesse, as high-tier Sorcery spells are game-changing and require heavy point investment.

## Key Abilities & Synergies

- **Longbow is Essential**: Many abilities in the Finesse tree are dedicated to the Longbow. Not using one means wasting a significant portion of your potential ability points.
- **Scatter Shot**: This Longbow ability is a game-changer for Finesse builds, causing an astronomical increase in damage potential.
  > [!TIP]
  > At point-blank range, hitting an enemy with all arrows from a single Scatter Shot can kill most targets instantly. Mastering positioning and footwork to utilize Scatter Shot on single or multiple targets is key to maximizing your DPS.
- **Weapon Synergy**: The **Blade Honing** ability also boosts critical damage for **Longswords and Greatswords**, making them the ideal melee weapon choices for a Finesse/Might hybrid.
transcription:
## Introduction to Finesse Builds

In this Kingdoms of Amalur: Re-Reckoning guide, we're going to be taking a look at Finesse builds: how to make a pure Finesse build, hybrid builds, and just having some general discussion about what sort of builds you can make based around Finesse. I'll be getting into some more specific build guides later on, but for now I just want to cover some basics and some direction that you should take if you're making a Finesse build.

## The Pure Finesse Destiny: Nightblade

First of all, let's take a look at the destinies. If you're gonna go the pure Finesse route, these are the sort of upgrades you're gonna get as you place more and more points into Finesse.

If you look all the way down at the bottom, you go to Nightblade. This is where you're going to cap out at 109 points. You're going to notice Assassination there, which gives you plus 300% damage, a guaranteed critical against an enemy if you've triggered an Evasion. So Evasion is basically like a passive chance there to avoid an attack if they hit you, try and hit you. It's just you have a chance to avoid it. You can increase this with one of the twists of fate to about 17% if I'm not mistaken. So you're gonna have about a 17% chance, assuming you get that, and that's basically what you're going to try and build around that concept if you're going to go the pure route here.

## Pure Finesse vs. Might Hybrid Destinies

You'll also notice looking over these destinies that you have a lot more bonus to ranged damage attack. Piercing is also ranged, it is also on Faeblades and daggers, but it's on longbows as well. So you're going to get more of a bonus to ranged attacks if you're playing a pure Finesse build than you're going to get towards melee. So if you want to melee and do ranged, well, you're probably going to take some sort of hybrid build because this is going to make you do ranged attacks a little bit better than melee.

Just taking a look over the Might/Finesse combination here, you'll see immediately you have plus 25% melee attack damage and plus 20% ranged. This is 10% less ranged in exchange for 25% more melee. You have the same critical chance, 5% less pierce damage, some damage from stealth. So if you want to play a stealth based build that's going to take people from stealth, this is a better pick than pure Finesse. And Cutthroat, which just gives you increased physical damage as a whole. So this build is a much better, or this type of build, is a much better bet if you want to mix melee and ranged. And pure Finesse is going to skew a little bit more towards the range department.

## Key Finesse Abilities & Weapon Synergies

If you look over the Finesse abilities, you're going to notice immediately there's a lot of bonuses in there that benefit the longbow. So one of your weapons, if you're going to play a Finesse build, or one that focuses highly on Finesse, should be a longbow. It's going to be an absolute waste if you don't do this because you have to spend a lot of ability points in order to get up in the tiers. So some of those are probably going to end up in longbows. If you're not using one, you're going to be wasting like 20 to 30 points in the longbow that that just frankly aren't doing use at all.

Additionally, if you're looking at doing some sort of hybrid build with melee, you'll notice that Blade Honing actually gives you increased critical damage with longswords and greatswords as well. So you're going to use probably one of those four weapon types: daggers, Faeblades, longswords, or greatswords if you're hybriding with a Might build in order to take best advantage of that. And then Envenomed Edge also says it applies to bladed weapons. So you're probably going, I don't know, I haven't tested it out to see if it actually works with hammers or not, but because Blade Honing already works with that, you're going to use the poison from that and the added critical bonus probably on one of those four weapon types.

## Core Finesse Combat Strategy: Poisons & Bleeds

The general concept when playing a pure Finesse build is that you're going to try and stack poisons and bleeds on enemies, and then melee them to death or stay back and pick them off with your bow, depending on what the scenario is.

You actually get some benefit later in the game that increase your poison and bleed damage, so you're always going to make sure you want to have poison and bleed on your targets, especially if they're hard to kill targets. And you also once you get Executioner, this is going to allow you to gain bonus damage against targets that have poison and bleeding on them, excuse me. So you're going to always at least minimally want to make sure they have a bleed, but poison helps as well. So if you can get like multiple dots on these guys, they're going to go down faster. That's kind of the strategy. You can do that with a bow or you can do it with your melee weapon. You can kind of like hang back and sort of, you know, lob some volleys in at range, get them bleeding and poisoned, and then go in for melee attacks.

## The Assassin/Might Hybrid Alternative

Now one of the builds I'm working on right now is actually taking the Assassin destiny instead of Nightblade, and then putting a bunch of points into Might as well. And this is because the Evasion chance, 17% or 11% depending on, you know, whether you've got that twist of fate or not, is RNG based, and you just don't know when it's going to happen or how often it's going to happen. So if you take one down from that, you're going to have a lot of, you're going to have like 33 extra points in Might to put however you want. That means you could use a different weapon type if you want, or you can get some bonuses to health, or you can take like Adrenaline Surge so you can get some more crit chance. There's just a lot of things you can do there. 

Additionally, another nice combo with Might is Concussive Force, which gives you increased damage against stunned enemies. And because you can set stunning with the trap in the Finesse line, or you can do it with the one of the end skills that makes it so that when you use poison abilities on an enemy you have a chance to set stunned. This works very, very well. So you can get stunned very easily and then you can deal increased damage, upping your damage output.

## Hybridizing Finesse with Sorcery

Now if you're talking about hybriding with Sorcery, I think probably what your main goal to do here would be either to add elemental damage, increased elemental damage to your bow, so your maybe has shocked or fire on it and you're going to increase that damage, or if you want to play a 100% range build. So you're going to take something like a staff or a scepter or chakrams and a bow and you're just going to use both of these and try and stay at range the whole time. 

And I think you could make a similar build using the Assassin setup instead of putting in might and going into sorcery. But I think generally speaking, if you're going to multi-class with Sorcery and Finesse or hybrid, whatever you want to call it, you're probably better off going mostly Sorcery and less Finesse, because some of the best spells are at the end, and you have to put a lot of points unnecessarily into this skill tree in order to get things unlocked that you need, and you just won't have that many points if you do it from the Finesse side.

Also, if you don't want to use Assassin for that sort of build, the Spellcloak is a very good choice. This is going to increase your elemental damage, piercing damage, which is bows and also Faeblades and them as well. And it gives you crit chance, mana restored, and it also allows you to guarantee a crit against enemies that are panicked. Enemies can be panicked when they're set on fire. It's just there's nice synergy there with fire spells. 

Again, the problem is getting enough points into Sorcery in order to boost your fire damage so that it becomes useful to try and set enemies on fire. I think the Spellcloak is probably a lot better if you're planning on using scepters for your other weapon because they consume mana to use them and that's going to give you the extra mana regeneration that you probably wouldn't otherwise need if you're not using scepters. If you're using like chakrams and a bow for a ranged build, you're not really going to consume much mana. You're not going to be like throwing out a lot of spells. So if it's particularly if you're going primarily Finesse, obviously if you're going primarily Sorcery that's a bit different, you're going probably use spells in there. If you're going primarily Finesse and just trying to work around the Finesse abilities and add some Sorcery, you're probably just going to try and boost your elemental damage and maybe have a couple buffs.

## Mastering the Longbow and Scatter Shot

One thing I want to mention particularly about Finesse builds, especially if you're using the longbow, which you should be if you're using Finesse, is that once you gain the Scatter Shot ability, your damage absolutely increases by an astronomical amount. If you can get point blank on an enemy with Scatter Shot and hit them with all arrows that you fire, you're going to be doing devastating damage. 

You should be using your charge shot all throughout the game even before you get Scatter Shot because your charge shot, you know, where you hold shoot until it like charges up and you fire it, is very very powerful and it's a much better way to use arrows. You generally can get the spacing in most fights in order to use it well, but it just deals a ton of damage. 

And once you get Scatter Shot, you know, learning to use Scatter Shot effectively is a huge part of playing a Finesse build, especially if you're using a bow again. Because not only if you hit something point blank is it probably dead in one or two shots, but also you can move the target that you're aiming at and maybe let's say you sidestep to your right a little bit and then another enemy gets in front of you. Now you're hitting the guy behind it and the guy in front of you at the same time. So learning like your footwork on where to position with Scatter Shot can really, really up your DPS with this build.

## Conclusion and What's Next

That pretty much wraps up the video for Finesse builds. We're going to be doing Might builds and Sorcery builds as well, so if you want to see my thoughts on those and how to make good builds with those, there's just some general information, be sure to check that out. 

Obviously, we'll be getting into some exact builds and some, you know, good setups that I think work well. I have some ideas for those already but I need to get a little bit higher levels. It's taking me a little bit longer than I want. If you want to stop by and ask questions or hang out, we're going to be on Twitch playing this week and next week, so be sure to drop by if you have more questions or head over to the wiki if you need more specific information.
